 Renewed flash flood threat targets Four Corners after rare severe weather slams Arizona
 The same system threatening Arizona will also soak parts of Southern California and create a low-end tornado risk across a corridor from Carmel southward to Los Angeles.
 By
 Julian Atienza 
 Source
 FOX Weather
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Email 
 Copy Link
 05:10 Rare severe storm threat targets Arizona with potential egg-sized hail, tornadoes 
 Severe thunderstorms are already blasting parts of Arizona early Wednesday ahead of a rare severe weather threat that will intensify through the day and into the evening. Parts of the state, including Flagstaff and Prescott, are under a Level 3 out of 5 risk of severe thunderstorms for  damaging egg-sized hail and tornadoes. A Flood Watch covers much of the state, as well as parts of southern Utah, southwestern Colorado and western New Mexico. 
 THE TAKEAWAY 
 A renewed flash flood threat is present in the Four Corners Thursday.
 Arizona was under a rare severe weather threat for large hail and tornadoes Wednesday.
 A Tornado Watch was issued in Arizona for the first time in over 15 years.
 Intense thunderstorms could also produce flash flooding.
 FLAGSTAFF, Ariz. — A renewed flash flood threat is present in the Four Corners Thursday after a day of severe thunderstorms that intensified through Wednesday evening.
 In southeastern Colorado, a small Level 3 out of 4 flash flood threat exists close to the Ferris Fire burn scar. The FOX Forecast Center said 3 to 5 inches of rain is possible.
 Parts of Arizona, including Flagstaff and Prescott, were under a Level 3 out of 5 risk of severe thunderstorms capable of producing damaging egg-sized hail and tornadoes on Wednesday. Flood Watches have been issued for the state through Thursday.
 WHAT IS A SUPERCELL THUNDERSTORM? 
 A strong storm system moving across the West Coast tapprf into a plume of humid air over Arizona Wednesday afternoon. The same system also soaked parts of Southern California and created a low-end tornado risk across a corridor from Carmel southward to Los Angeles.  
 A Tornado Watch was issued in the state of Arizona for the first time in 16 years, according to the FOX Forecast Center .
 Severe weather threat
 (FOX Weather) 
  Rain began Wednesday afternoon across Southern California, causing flash flooding, particularly over wildfire burn scars.
 Meanwhile, parts of Central Arizona were under a Level 3 severe weather threat, which hasn't happened in October since NOAA moved to a five-tiered risk scale in 2015.
 A Tornado Warning was issued for part of Yavapai County on Wednesday morning.
 Flash flood threat
 (FOX Weather) 
  There was also a Severe Thunderstorm Watch in effect for Arizona, and a Level 2 severe storm threat covering Phoenix, Glendale, Chandler and Scottsdale.
 A Flood Watch was issued for much of the state, as well as parts of southern Utah, southwestern Colorado and western New Mexico. More thunderstorms could develop Thursday as the system shifts east toward the Rockies.
 Hail threat
 (FOX Weather) 
  Arizona and other parts of the Southwest generally see most of their severe weather during monsoon season, which typically runs from mid-June to the end of September.
 These storms could signal a larger pattern of increased storminess and severe weather across the Southern Tier of the country that could unfold this winter due to an impending Super El Niño. During Super El Niño years, the jet stream usually shifts directly over the southern U.S., acting as an atmospheric conveyor belt for storms and leading to flooding and severe weather outbreaks.
 Super El Niño impacts
 (FOX Weather) 
  According to the FOX Forecast Center, two of the past three super El Niño winters, 1997-1998 and 2015–2016, have brought significant severe storm outbreaks mainly across the Gulf Coast, Southeast and Southern Plains.
